title: Matrix sign of a zero-diagonal block recovers the principal square root
expression_sketch:
Let A, B lie in C^{n x n} and suppose AB (equivalently BA) has no eigenvalues on the closed negative real axis R-. Then the 2n x 2n block P = [[0, A], [B, 0]] has no pure imaginary eigenvalues, and
  sign(P) = [[0, C], [C^{-1}, 0]],    C = A (BA)^{-1/2},
where (BA)^{-1/2} is the principal inverse square root. The special case B = I and A with no eigenvalues on R- is
  sign([[0, A], [I, 0]]) = [[0, A^{1/2}], [A^{-1/2}, 0]].
On a single matrix with no pure imaginary eigenvalues the same square-root representation collapses to the concise identity sign(A) = A (A^2)^{-1/2}, equivalently the Roberts integral
  sign(A) = (2/pi) A Integral((t^2 I + A^2)^{-1}, (t, 0, infinity)).
When AB meets R- the block P meets iR and sign(P) is not defined.
latent_structure: One MATRIX_FUNCTION master, the primary sign of a 2n block with zero diagonal blocks, produces principal square roots of BA (and of A when B = I) as off-diagonal blocks. The scalar kernel z |-> z/(z^2)^{1/2} on the spectrum of A is the same object. The undefined stratum is imaginary-axis spectrum of P, equivalently negative-real spectrum of AB.

t.note: dummy of the Roberts integral on [0, infinity)

function_domains.sign: Primary matrix sign, defined precisely when the argument has no pure imaginary eigenvalues (Higham Ch. 5 opening paragraph and Theorem 5.1).
function_domains.principal_square_root: For a matrix with no eigenvalues on R-, the unique square root whose spectrum lies in the open right half-plane (Higham Theorem 1.29). Written X^{1/2}.

nonzero_conditions.statement: A having no pure imaginary eigenvalues implies A is nonsingular (Higham Ch. 5, paragraph before (5.1)).
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Chapter 5, paragraph before (5.1) and Theorem 5.1

analytic_domains.statement: A in C^{n x n} has no pure imaginary eigenvalues whenever sign(A) is invoked (Higham Theorem 5.1 hypothesis).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 5.1 and equations (5.1)--(5.3)

analytic_domains.statement: A, B in C^{n x n} and AB (hence also BA) has no eigenvalues on R- (Higham Theorem 5.2 hypothesis). Then P = [[0, A], [B, 0]] has no pure imaginary eigenvalues, so sign(P) is defined.
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 5.2; Higham, Mackey, Mackey, Tisseur, SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 26 (2005)

analytic_domains.statement: A having no pure imaginary eigenvalues is equivalent to A^2 having no eigenvalues on R-, so the principal inverse square root (A^2)^{-1/2} in sign(A) = A (A^2)^{-1/2} is defined (Higham, text between (5.2) and (5.3)).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, text between (5.2) and (5.3)

branch_conventions: Principal square root: unique primary square root with spectrum in the open right half-plane (Higham Theorem 1.29).
Scalar sign: sign(z) = 1 if Re z > 0 and sign(z) = -1 if Re z < 0; undefined on iR (Higham Ch. 5 opening display).
sign(A) is a primary matrix function of A, hence a polynomial in A, but it is in general a nonprimary square root of I (Higham, paragraph after Theorem 5.1).

limit_domains.statement: The Roberts integral parameter t runs over the improper interval [0, infinity). The integrand (t^2 I + A^2)^{-1} is defined for all t >= 0 precisely because A^2 has no eigenvalues on R- (Higham (5.3) and Problem 5.3).
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, equation (5.3) and Problem 5.3

derived_conditions.statement: If P = [[0, A], [B, 0]] had a pure imaginary eigenvalue then P^2 = diag(AB, BA) would have an eigenvalue on R-; the Theorem 5.2 hypothesis on AB therefore implies sign(P) is defined (Higham, proof of Theorem 5.2).
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 5.2 proof

derived_conditions.statement: C D = I in the block formula, so the lower-left block of sign(P) is C^{-1} (Higham, proof of Theorem 5.2, using S^2 = I from Theorem 5.1(a)).
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 5.1(a) and Theorem 5.2 proof

why_not_cse_lgg: The block identity equates a 2n primary sign evaluation to a pair of n x n principal roots. CSE will not invent that the off-diagonal blocks of sign(P) are C and C^{-1}. LGG will not identify sign of a zero-diagonal block as a master for square roots, nor treat the AB-meets-R- stratum as a change of representation rather than an undefined evaluation.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide sign, csgn, principal square root, Roberts integral, involutory. Catalog members are the expanded block array of sign(P), the formula A (A^2)^{-1/2}, and the real-line integral kernel (t^2 I + A^2)^{-1}.
notes: Do not insert self-adjointness or positive-definiteness of A or B; Theorem 5.2 is for general complex A, B. Do not replace the real-line integral (5.3) by a closed-contour calculus of a general f. Do not replace the principal square root by an arbitrary square root of BA. Imaginary-axis eigenvalues are excluded by the cited hypotheses, not by folklore broadening.
